speaker: Sheldon
text: Right, one bacon cheeseburger, breaking two Jewish dietary restrictions simultaneously. Kudos. Beer battered fish and chips. Now, here's your tartar sauce. I also brought you salsa. It's a little unconventional, but I think you'll like it. It's zingy. And for you, factory burrito grande, no cheese, no sour cream, no ugly consequences of your lactose intolerance. Bon appétit.

speaker: Leonard
text: Hang on. Black beans, not pinto beans? Double guacamole? No cilantro? Lettuce shredded, not chopped? You understand why I'm doing this to you? That'll be all. That was fun.

speaker: Sheldon
text: How long can you keep this up?

speaker: Leonard
text: I heard about this professor at MIT who melted down, bought a van, and spent the rest of his life as a mobile dog groomer.

text: He never went back to the university?

speaker: Leonard
text: Only to shampoo Professor Shamburg's Shih Tzu.

text: I bet if we all chipped in, we could buy a show in the van.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, that's the only thing wrong with that plan.

text: Hey, guys, sorry you had to wait, but we are swamped. What's this? Shelton doesn't work here.

text: Well, honey, not to complain, but we were starting to think you didn't either.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Is that really necessary? Good Lord. The interference pattern in the fracture. The motion of the wave through the molecular structure. I've been looking at it all wrong. I can't consider the electrons as particles. They move through the graphene as a wave.

text: It's a wave! The moment to applaud would be now.
